queries.query_text: human tumor tissue metabolomics immune checkpoint inhibitor short chain fatty acids inosine mass spectrometry
What are the absolute concentrations of gut microbiota-derived metabolites like butyrate and inosine in human tumor microenvironment samples from patients responding to immunotherapy?

still_missing: The gap requires primary studies reporting absolute quantitative concentrations of microbial metabolites measured directly in human tumor tissue (TME) or paired tumor-serum samples. This study only reports serum levels (relative comparisons, no absolute values provided in text) and does not provide measurements from human tumor tissue biopsies.
usable_content: The study performed targeted metabolomics (GC-MS/MS) on serum samples from NSCLC patients treated with anti-PD-1 therapy. It reported that responders had significantly higher serum levels of acetic acid, propionic acid, and butyric acid compared to non-responders. The study also found a positive correlation between serum butyric acid levels and PD-1 expression on circulating CD8+ T cells. Mechanistic experiments in vitro and in vivo demonstrated that butyrate enhances anti-PD-1 efficacy by promoting histone H3K27 acetylation at the Pdcd1 and Cd28 promoters in CD8+ T cells and enhancing TCR signaling (PLCγ1 phosphorylation). The study is a review summarizing the biochemical properties, sources, and signaling pathways of inosine, a microbial metabolite. It details mechanisms by which inosine (produced by bacteria like Bifidobacterium pseudolongum) enhances anti-tumor immunity via A2A receptor-mediated T cell activation and macrophage polarization in preclinical CRC models. It also describes pro-tumorigenic roles where inosine serves as a carbon source for cancer cells or promotes EMT. The review mentions one Phase II clinical trial evaluating oral inosine combined with PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors and chemotherapy in a mixed solid tumor population, noting it mildly enhanced efficacy and reduced toxicity, but explicitly states that CRC-specific results were not reported separately.
